correctness.rationale: Exact exponential integral calculations verify all finite identities; exhaustive n=2,3 rank permutations reproduce E L, E A and E LA. value.rationale: The departure of one participant from a random two-sided preference matrix is a natural structural stability problem. The birth population has a Poisson quarter marginal, yet losing the deleted row’s reciprocal match amplifies expected replacement births elevenfold, 11/24 versus 1/24, a dependence not inferable from marginal tables. Exact finite covariance and an explicit joint law capture the redistribution of reciprocity, with plausible use in model calibration and deletion sensitivity.
